newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian negotiator heads to Chile for trade deal.
newsitem.headline: Canadian negotiator heads to Chile for trade deal.

text.p: Canadian International Trade Minister Art Eggleton said on Thursday that Canada's chief negotiator of a free trade agreement with Chile would head to Santiago on Friday to try to conclude the deal.

Eggleton said he spoke with his Chilean counterpart today and hoped to wrap up an agreement over the next few days ahead of a visit to Ottawa by Chilean President Eduardo Frei. Frei is due to arrive in Canada on November 17.
"I'm still optimistic," Eggleton told reporters after a cabinet meeting.
The chief negotiator for Canada is Keith Christie.
Eggleton has delined to confirm Chilean assertions that Canada agreed to a Chilean rule requiring foreign investors to deposit about 30 percent of their funds with Chile's central bank.
Ottawa had wanted an exemption from the rule, which was one of the few unresolved issues in the last stages of negotiations.
